conv:debug@local.text: Focus AI (fallback): Newton's second law states that force equals mass times acceleration (F = m * a). In simple terms: the acceleration of an object depends on the net force acting on it and its mass. Example: pushing a shopping cart harder (more force) makes it speed up more; pushing two carts tied together (more mass) gives less acceleration for same force. Summary: F = m·a. Practice: If a 2 kg object accelerates at 3 m/s², what's the force? (Answer: 6 N).
